pointers.sentence: A backend quotes a name by wrapping it and escapes no quotation mark inside it (`django/db/backends/postgresql/operations.py:DatabaseOperations.quote_name`), so a quotation mark would end the name early: the defence is to refuse such a name before it is written.
Each fix also went to 4.2's patch releases 4.2.15 to 4.2.28 (`docs/releases/4.2.15.txt`, `docs/releases/4.2.28.txt`).

It raises `ValueError` where `FORBIDDEN_ALIAS_PATTERN` finds a quotation mark (SQLite's square brackets among them), whitespace, a control character, a semicolon, a hash or a comment marker (`django/db/models/sql/query.py:Query.check_alias`; [The SELECT clause: `get_select`, the select mask and `klass_info`](../sql/select.md#annotations-and-extras-the-masks)).

The name of a `FilteredRelation` is the alias of the table its join brings in, which `Join.as_sql` writes after the table (`django/db/models/sql/datastructures.py:Join.as_sql`; [`filter`, `exclude` and `Q` objects](../querysets/filters.md#filteredrelation-a-condition-in-the-join)).

The period's refusal came with CVE-2026-1312 (5.2.11, 6.0.2), whose notes say `QuerySet.order_by` "was subject to SQL injection in column aliases containing periods" when a `FilteredRelation` used the same alias (`docs/releases/5.2.11.txt`).
At this commit it does so only for one that did (`django/db/models/sql/query.py:Query.add_filtered_relation`, `django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLCompiler._order_by_pairs`).
At this commit it does so only for one that did (`django/db/models/sql/query.py:Query.add_filtered_relation`, `django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLCompiler._order_by_pairs`).

6.1 quotes the alias of every table and join with `SQLCompiler.quote_name`, and PostgreSQL's backend lost its own compiler for a SELECT (`django/db/backends/postgresql/compiler.py`; [What changed in expressions, lookups and the compiler](sql.md)).

`Q.__init__` takes two keyword arguments of its own, `"_connector"` and `"_negated"`, and the connector is the word `WhereNode.as_sql` writes between the conditions it joins (`django/db/models/sql/where.py:WhereNode.as_sql`).

The fix guards twice: `QuerySet._filter_or_exclude_inplace` refuses both keywords with `TypeError`, by `PROHIBITED_FILTER_KWARGS`, and `Q` refuses with `ValueError` any connector but `Q.AND`, `Q.OR`, `Q.XOR` and `None` (`django/db/models/query.py:QuerySet._filter_or_exclude_inplace`; [`filter`, `exclude` and `Q` objects](../querysets/filters.md#the-two-keyword-arguments-that-are-refused)).

6.1 carried the guard further, which no note lists: `Q._check_connector` also checks the connector given to `Q.create`, a class method by which Django builds `Q` objects of its own, with `Q.AND`, `Q.OR`, `Q.XOR`, the connector of a `Q` it copies, or none (`django/db/models/query_utils.py:Q._check_connector`).

5.2.17 and 6.0.8 handed them to its `Q`, so `When` could be given `"_negated"`: `When(title="Dawn", _negated=True, then=Value(1))` there marked every entry but Dawn (`django/db/models/expressions.py:When.__init__`).

Before 5.0.10 and 5.1.4 a `HasKey` made directly on Oracle "was subject to SQL injection if untrusted data was used as a lhs value"; `"has_key"` through the double-underscore syntax was not, the notes say (CVE-2024-53908; `docs/releases/5.0.10.txt`).

`HasKeyLookup.compile_json_path_final_key` writes the key through `json.dumps`, which escapes U+FFFF, so a key cannot close the literal (`django/db/models/fields/json.py:HasKeyLookup.as_oracle`, `django/db/models/fields/json.py:HasKeyLookup.compile_json_path_final_key`).

A raster lookup on PostGIS may carry a band index in its value (`django/contrib/gis/db/models/lookups.py:GISLookup.process_band_indices`), and `PostGISOperator.check_raster` writes the index into the SQL.

Since 5.2.11 and 6.0.2 (CVE-2026-1207) it raises `TypeError` for an index that is not an integer (`django/contrib/gis/db/backends/postgis/operations.py:PostGISOperator.check_raster`; [Spatial lookups, functions and distances](../contrib/spatial-queries.md)).
